A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Poly2Vec framework and authorship. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable, allowing reliable comparison despite substantial restructuring and replacement of experiments.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic and California experiments on topology classification, distance estimation, nearest-neighbor search, cross-geometry generalization and fusion ablations, including appendix results.

after.justification: v2 reports original Singapore and New York experiments on spatial relationships, population prediction and land use inference, plus frequency-sampling and fusion ablations in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The central Fourier encoding and magnitude/phase fusion remain. Polygon triangulation changes from ear clipping to constrained Delaunay. The topology predictor changes from sigmoid of an embedding dot product with binary cross-entropy to concatenated embeddings processed by an MLP with cross-entropy. These are limited procedural changes around the retained encoder; the new RegionDCL integration also replaces its original features and removes distance bias.

E1.justification: v1's synthetic geometries and California landmarks, roads, lakes and parks are replaced by Singapore/New York POIs, roads and buildings. v2 adds 16-direction classification, multiclass topology for polygon-involving pairs, population prediction and land use inference. Nearest-neighbor retrieval and the explicit cross-geometry transfer scenarios are removed. This substantially changes both represented populations and task requirements.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated TILE, WRAP and GRID baselines, and T2VEC for polyline comparisons; v1 cited T2VEC but did not evaluate it. RegionDCL and its distance-bias removal control are new application comparators. Coord/DIRECT and NUFT/NUFTSPEC represent corresponding retained baselines rather than additions; THEORY and RESNET1D also remain.

E3.justification: v2 reports 5,000 topology pairs per class, versus 10,000 in v1 Section 4.2.1, and introduces position-adjusted pair generation and multiclass evaluation. Classification reporting changes from AUROC/weighted F1 to accuracy, precision, recall and F1. Distance evaluation changes from MSE to MAE, and point-polyline targets change from nearest-point distance to centroid distance. Maximum sampled frequency changes from 5.0 to 1.0. The 60:20:20 split and core spatial-task training budget remain.

E4.justification: v1's cross-geometry generalization study, including Appendix A.3, is removed. Its nearest-neighbor fusion ablation is replaced by fusion ablations across topology, direction and distance tasks in v2 Figures 4 and 6–9. v2 additionally tests learned versus fixed frequencies in Appendix A.3.2 and removes RegionDCL's distance bias as an application-level control. These substantially revise the questions investigated.

E5.justification: v1 reports point estimates without run counts or uncertainty estimates. v2 Appendix A.4.3 newly specifies five runs for spatial-reasoning experiments, and its spatial and GeoAI result tables report means and standard deviations. This substantially expands uncertainty reporting; it does not establish that v1 used fewer runs.

E6.justification: The synthetic/California results are replaced by Singapore/New York results, with new directional and GeoAI outcomes and removal of retrieval/transfer results. For example, v2 Table 4 reports Singapore population MAE of 5807.54 for RegionDCL versus 4957.58 with Poly2Vec, and New York land-use L1 of 0.418 versus 0.397. These are new within-v2 comparisons, not performance gains over v1 under matched conditions.

T1.justification: v2 adds explicit encoding properties, including monotonic distance preservation, and intermediate Fourier derivations while retaining most underlying mathematics. Some equations change non-equivalently: the final line-segment formula in Appendix A.2.2 uses inverse squared-length scaling, whereas v1 Equation 17 and v2 Equation 10 use squared-length scaling. Thus the mathematical revision includes a new internal inconsistency, not merely relocated notation.

C1.justification: The unified encoding and learned-fusion contributions remain, but the headline claims expand substantially. v1 emphasizes consistent spatial-reasoning performance; v2 claims superiority across topology, direction and distance tasks and improved population prediction and land use inference through GeoAI integration. The abstract, introduction and conclusion now make practical workflow benefits a central contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations linking directional errors to grid discretization, interprets the RegionDCL experiment as showing that encoded spatial information can replace distance bias, and argues that learned frequencies offer little benefit. It removes v1's discussion of global Fourier features limiting nearest-point distance estimation and its interpretation of transfer from complex to simpler geometries. These materially change the explanatory and applicability discussion.

D1.justification: v2 Appendix A.4 adds dataset counts, OSM extraction tags and format, geographic boundary sources, land-use/population label sources, class aggregation and pair-generation instructions, alongside fuller baseline descriptions. Hardware, software and several training settings are retained and relocated. v1's explicit hidden-layer width and Douglas-Peucker tolerances are no longer documented. GeoAI training details are largely delegated to the cited RegionDCL work.

R1.justification: Research positioning expands from mixed-geometry spatial reasoning to preserving coordinate information within GeoAI and future foundation models. v2 adds substantial literature on GeoAI applications, region representation, foundation models, point encoders and PolygonGNN. Some earlier interlinking, nearest-neighbor and polygon-coding references disappear, while the principal Fourier and polygon-encoding antecedents remain.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, methods, experimental narrative and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Evaluation is organized around four research questions and separated into spatial reasoning and GeoAI integration. Detailed derivations, normalization and experimental settings move into expanded appendices. These are substantial narrative and organizational changes beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: v2 adopts an ICML-style layout, redraws the Fourier illustration and workflow, and consolidates the affine-transformation diagrams into Figure 2. Result tables are extensively restructured, including uncertainty values. Distance scatter plots, directional/application tables and broader ablation figures replace or supplement v1's distance bars, retrieval tables and transfer plots, substantially changing the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's limited evidence of usefulness in complete GeoAI workflows: Section 4.2 and Table 4 provide controlled population and land-use comparisons, supported by broader baselines and newly reported uncertainty. The added data-construction details and targeted ablations also strengthen assessability. These gains outweigh the loss of cross-geometry transfer tests and the new main-text/appendix formula inconsistency, although those weaknesses limit confidence in generalization claims and mathematical reproducibility.
